items.line: Ein anderer Gegensatz ist בת כרכבי und בת עורבתי (s. B. Batra 91, a).
items.note: The disputed slot seems to be the first Hebrew name, after 'ist בת', where the base line has כרכבי. The print there appears to read כרנבו (Karnebo, as in B. Batra 91a); the second name reads עורבתי. It is not certain which slot the two readings refer to.

items.line: Ein anderer Gegensatz ist בת כרכבי und בת עורבתי (s. B. Batra 91, a).
items.note: The first Hebrew word after 'ist בת' reads right to left as כ-ר-נ-כ-ו. The third letter is clearly נ (not כ) and the last is ו (not י). The fourth letter looks like a rounded כ, though it may be a ב (the Talmudic name is כרנבו), so that letter is uncertain.

items.line: Grube, in welcher der Jäger sich verborgen hält: כוך (Tanit 22, a).
items.note: The final letter is a plain descender with no inner hook, so it is final kaf (ך) rather than final pe (ף). It differs visibly from the ף in צריף on the line above.

items.note: The letter after ט is printed as a full-height vertical stroke, i.e. ו rather than the short י, which gives אשטור. This matches the transliteration Astur.

items.line: an dem Hinterkopf, eine Mündung, die תורבץ הושט heißt, sie besteht
items.note: The line reads תורבץ, then the gullet word. After the ה there is a small mark plus a full vav, which I take as a double vav (הוושט, the usual spelling), but it could be a speck before a single vav (הושט). The two OCR readings mostly match words from the next line (מחקשה, דריוש), not this one.

items.line: (וושט) hat bei seinem Beginn, d. i., bei seinem Anfang unmittelbar
items.note: Inside the parentheses I see ט, a wide ש, and what looks like a single ו before the closing parenthesis. The print is small and the ש may be crowding a second ו, so a doubled וו cannot be ruled out.

items.note: The fourth letter is not ט: it has the open two-legged shape of ת/ח, unlike the ט in the same word in line 1. I read it as ת, but the left foot that would separate ת from ח is hard to make out at this resolution. The second letter is a small, dot-like י.

items.line: Beweis liefert Raschi mit seinen eigenen Worten, indem er sagt: איסטומכא אני
items.note: The third letter appears open on the left like כ, not a closed ס. In the next line, by contrast, איסתומכא has a clear closed ס. The small yod after א is faint and looks like an apostrophe, which lowers confidence.

items.line: dritten Magen verschiedentlich benannt, und zwar כרם, סניא דיבי,
items.note: The last letter of the word looks squared with a flat base, like final mem (ם). It seems to differ from the rounder samekh in the nearby סניא and דכרסא, which suggests a misprint for כרס. The scan resolution leaves some doubt.

items.line: פטרוכא, von hier in den עיזקתא, von hier aus endlich geschieht die
items.note: The word is printed twice: once in the line beginning פטרוכא and again after 'Was'. Both look like ע-י-ז-ק-ת-א, which matches the Aramaic word for 'ring' and the 'ringelartige Rundung' in the text. The third letter looks like ז rather than ו, and a short letter is visible there, so the עיקתא reading seems wrong. The ת vs ח distinction is not certain at this resolution.
